instruction.text: Many global goods are manufactured in Germany. Match each product to the correct image.

feedback.finish: Germany has one of the world’s largest economies, which is primarily driven by its manufacturing sector.

hint.text: There are more bikes than people in the Netherlands!
hint.label: Did you know?

atoms.b: The Netherlands is a very ((++low-lying round)) nation, with around one third of its land being below sea level.
In the 1970s, the Dutch government listened to public calls for better road safety and created a network of new ((++bike boat)) paths.
Paired with the country’s ((++flat bumpy)) terrain, cycling has become the easiest and most popular way of getting around.

instruction.text: Read the text and select the matching image.

atoms.a: The Alps are the largest mountain range in Europe. Its tallest mountain is Mont Blanc, which borders both France and Italy.
atoms.sound: The Alps are the largest mountain range in Europe. Its tallest mountain is Mont Blonc, which borders both France and Italy.

atoms.a: Every year, 120 million tourists visit the Alps to take part in winter sports like skiing.
The Alpine ibex can be found living on the steep mountain terrain of the Alps.
The alphorn was traditionally used to communicate across the valleys of the Alps. Today, it is more of a ceremonial instrument.

trainers.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: Épernay and Bordeaux are French cities both renowned for their wine. However, the types of wine they produce differ due to their climates.
atoms.sound: Épanay and Bordeaux are French cities both renowned for their wine. However, the types of wine they produce differ due to their climates.

atoms.text: The cooler, northern climate of Épernay produces a more acidic grape as the fruit gets a lot less sun and tends to not be as ripe. This is perfect for making a sparkling wine called champagne.
atoms.sound: The cooler, northern climate of Épanay produces a more acidic grape as the fruit gets a lot less sun and tends to not be as ripe. This is perfect for making a sparkling wine called champagne.

atoms.text: The climate in the region around Bordeaux is much warmer all year round, producing riper more flavourful grapes. Its proximity to the Atlantic Ocean also helps regulate temperatures, preventing both freezing winters and scorching summers.

atoms.a: Which French cities are renowned for their wine?
Why are the grapes in the north of France more acidic?
b: ++The north of France gets less sun, so the grapes do not become as ripe.
The north of France gets less sun, and frost makes the grapes sour.
The north of France has a lot more rain, which makes the grapes acidic.

atoms.a: Why is Bordeaux a suitable location for growing grapes?
b: ++The Atlantic Ocean helps to keep a good temperature year round.
The Pacific Ocean helps to keep a good temperature year round.
The Mediterranean Sea helps to keep a good temperature year round.
